units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 26:11">Targ. Prov. XXVI, 11</cite> <he>תְּיוּבֵיה</he> (Ms. <he>תיובת׳</he>).
Targ. Job XXIV, 23 (ed. Lag. תִּיבוּתָא).—Esp. = h. תְּשׁוּבָה return to God, repentance.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 33:6">Targ. Jer. XXXIII, 6</cite> (ed. Wil. <cite ref="V00424"><he>תִּיוּבָא</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Song of Songs 5:5">Targ. Cant. V, 5</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Taanit 23b:7">Taan. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>אנא בעי</he> … <he>דליהדרו בת׳</he> I prayed that they might die, but she prayed that they might return in repentance (<cite ref="Berakhot 10a:3">Ber. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>דלהדרו בתשובה</he>); a. e.—V. <cite ref="V01117"><he>תְּתוּבָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 12:5">Targ. Jer. XII, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 32:3">Targ. Job XXXII, 3</cite>; <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 32:5">5</cite>; a. e.—

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 16a:16">B. Mets. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>הא גברא והא ת׳</he> here is the man, and here is his answer (such an ingenious answer only such a man can give); <he>גברא קא חזינא ות׳ וכ׳</he> I see the man, but I do not see the answer (his argument does not convince me).

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 68a:4-5">Ab. Zar. 68ᵃ</cite> <he>חגא</he> … <he>ת׳ קא מותיב</he> Ḥagga knows not what the Rabbis say, and dares to argue? <cite ref="Berakhot 10b:34">Ber. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ דרב חסדא ת׳</he> this is an argument against Rab Ḥisda; it is an argument (R. Ḥ. stands refuted).
<cite ref="Berakhot 21a:6">Ib. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>ת׳</he> this is a final refutation; a. v. fr.—Pl. <he>תְּיוּבָתָא</he>.
Targ. Job XXI, 34 Ms. (ed. sing.).

senses.gloss: pl. as ab. going to and fro, waywardness.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 5:6">Targ. Jer. V, 6</cite> (ed. Wil. <cite ref="V00164"><he>תִּיוּ׳</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 14:7">Ib. XIV, 7</cite> <he>תְּיוּבָתָנָא</he> (not <he>תְּיוּבְתָּ׳</he>); a. e.
